notice: Candidate assessment definitions for the v0.3.0 lesson (Curriculum Excellence Standard V1). Unreviewed and unreleased: nothing scores them, writes mastery from them or releases them. Teacher-administered on paper or in class until a qualified reviewer approves them and a governed release binds them. Keys and scoring guides are reviewer only and must never reach a learner projection, offline package or client bundle.

tasks.fallbackRoute: Before the chart scene, rebuild the thousands period with counters on a paper chart (MOE Grade 4 numeration), then re-check with two similar numbers.
Fold a paper strip into ten equal parts and shade five; then fold each tenth into ten to show 50 hundredths. Re-check with 0.3.
Do the counter-exchange activity (ten counters become one in the next column) before the ten-times scene, then re-check with 4 × 10, 4 × 100, 4 × 1,000.

tasks.prompt: Write in standard form: four hundred sixty thousand, three and twenty-five thousandths.
tasks.note: Within MOE scope (hundred thousands and thousandths), so it survives a decision against the millions extension.

tasks.prompt: In 135,276.049, write the value of the 3 and the value of the 4.
Kebeh says 0.7 is less than 0.65 because 65 is bigger than 7. Is she right? Explain using place value, and show one way to check your answer.

scoringGuide.2: Says Kebeh is wrong and justifies by place: 7 tenths is more than 6 tenths, or 0.70 is more than 0.65 when both are written to hundredths; gives a check (chart, number line or hundredths grid).
scoringGuide.1: Correct decision with a vague or partly correct reason, or a correct reason with no check.
scoringGuide.0: Agrees with Kebeh, or no place-value reasoning.

tasks.prompt: The digit 5 appears three times in 505.05. Write what each 5 is worth. Then explain how the value of the first 5 compares with the value of the 5 in the ones place.

scoringGuide.2: 500, 5 and 0.05, and explains that 500 is 100 times 5 because it is two places to the left (each place is ten times the place to its right).
scoringGuide.1: All three values correct with no explanation of the relationship, or a correct relationship with one value wrong.
scoringGuide.0: Gives 5 for every digit, or no relationship stated.

tasks.prompt: Draw a number line from 2.3 to 2.4 and mark it in hundredths. Place 2.35 and 2.305 on it. Which one is closer to 2.3? Explain how the number line shows it.

scoringGuide.2: 2.35 at the halfway mark, 2.305 between 2.30 and 2.31; says 2.305 is closer to 2.3 and explains using the marks (2.305 is less than one hundredth away; 2.35 is five hundredths away).
scoringGuide.1: Correct answer with an imprecise placement or explanation.
scoringGuide.0: Says 2.35 is closer, or places 2.305 beyond 2.35.

tasks.note: New representation: the lesson uses charts and grids, never a number line.

tasks.prompt: Without notes: (a) What is the value of the 9 in 293,400.6? (b) Write 3.046 in expanded form. (c) Order 0.08, 0.8 and 0.088 from least to greatest and explain how you decided.
tasks.key: (a) 90,000 (b) 3 + 0.04 + 0.006 (c) 0.08, 0.088, 0.8; the explanation compares tenths first, then hundredths and thousandths

scoringGuide.4: (a), (b) and (c) correct with a place-value explanation

scoringGuide.2: 0.6, explained by tenths (6 tenths > 5 tenths) or by writing 0.600

tasks.prompt: Use each of the digits 0, 3, 5 and 8 exactly once, and one decimal point, to make the number closest to 5. Explain why no other arrangement is closer.

scoringGuide.2: 5.038 with an argument from the left: 5 ones first, then the smallest possible tenths (0), hundredths (3) and thousandths (8)
scoringGuide.1: 5.038 without a complete argument, or 5.083 with place-value reasoning

tasks.note: Optional and non-gating; the in-lesson challenge scene rehearses the same reasoning with different digits.
